code.originalText: Two-week review of the headache diary, the MRI and the comprehensive eye examination, seen the same day by headache medicine: diagnosis, withdrawal of the overused tablets and preventive treatment

text.paragraph: Two-week review of the headache diary, the MRI and the eye examination, seen the same day by headache medicine. [S]

Mr. Nietzsche returns with his 14-day headache diary, after an MRI and blood tests this morning and a comprehensive eye examination, and is seen by Dr. Achterberg-Sato of headache medicine on the same day. His diary shows headache on 10 of 14 days. On 7 of them the pain was moderate or severe, throbbing, mostly over the right forehead and eye, worse with walking uphill or reading, with light and noise sensitivity and nausea, and vomiting on 3; it lasted from six hours to most of two days. On the other 3 days the headache was a milder pressure across the forehead. He has had no visual or other aura. He took the butalbital combination on 9 days, two or three tablets each time, and ibuprofen on 2 more, so acute medicine on 11 of 14 days. By his account he has had headache on about 20 days a month for at least eight months, and has taken the combination tablets on most of those days. He has slept four to five hours a night. He has had no weakness, numbness, fever or change in his usual vision. [S]

Cranial nerves otherwise normal; strength, sensation, reflexes, coordination and gait normal; no papilledema

list.item:
Chronic migraine without aura (G43.709). Dr. Achterberg-Sato confirms chronic migraine by ICHD-3 criteria: headache on 15 or more days a month for more than three months, with migraine features on at least 8 days a month. The MRI with and without contrast shows no structural cause, including no mass behind the right eye, and the neurological examination is normal. Syphilis serology drawn this morning is nonreactive, so infection does not explain the unequal pupils, which date from early childhood, or the poor right eye, which the eye examination explains. With about 20 headache days a month and a MIDAS of 74, prevention is indicated. [S]
Galcanezumab 240 mg loading dose given today, then 120 mg every four weeks.
Naproxen 500 mg with metoclopramide 10 mg early in an attack, no more than two days a week.
Sumatriptan to be added once the taper is complete.

Medication overuse headache (G44.40). Regular use of a combination analgesic on 10 or more days a month for more than three months, with headache on 15 or more days, meets ICHD-3 criteria for medication overuse headache. Butalbital is a barbiturate and is tapered rather than stopped abruptly. [S]
Stop ibuprofen; replace as-needed combination tablets with a scheduled three-week taper: one tablet twice a day for a week, once a day for a week, every other day for a week, then stop.
Expect worse headache for one to two weeks; call the same day for tremor, sweating, agitation, confusion or a seizure.
Nurse phone check at the end of the first taper week.

Pathologic myopia of the right eye (H44.2E1). Myopic macular atrophy explains the long-standing poor vision in the right eye; there is no choroidal neovascularization or retinal break. The difference of about seven dioptres between the eyes makes spectacles uncomfortable. [S]
Contact lens fitting for both eyes.
Amsler grid for the right eye weekly.
Same-day eye care for new flashes, a shower of floaters, a shadow or distorted vision.

Chronic insomnia (G47.00). Four to five hours of sleep; no sedatives are to be added. [S]
CBT-I through the clinic's behavioral sleep program, starting next week.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society (IHS). The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (2018); The American Headache Society Consensus Statement: Update on integrating new migraine treatments into clinical practice (2021); Calcitonin gene-related peptide-targeting therapies are a first-line option for the prevention of migraine: An American Headache Society position statement update (2024); European Academy of Neurology guideline on the management of medication-overuse headache (2020); European Headache Federation guideline on the use of monoclonal antibodies targeting the calcitonin gene related peptide pathway for migraine prevention - 2022 update (2022); Choosing wisely in headache medicine: the American Headache Society's list of five things physicians and patients should question (2013); Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021 (2021); Refractive Errors Preferred Practice Pattern (2023); Comprehensive Adult Medical Eye Evaluation Preferred Practice Pattern (2026); Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline (2021)

Follow-up: Nurse phone check at the end of the first taper week. Four-week review with the second galcanezumab injection. Call the same day for withdrawal symptoms, a headache unlike his usual attacks, weakness, numbness, fever, or new flashes or floaters. Next scheduled visit 1881-08-18: four-week review after starting galcanezumab and the taper: withdrawal, headache days, acute medicine and the second injection. [S]
